chapter: Early career, theaters and Cobb's Tea Room
title: Directing silent-film scores at the Liberty Theater
summary: As leader of the Liberty Theater orchestra he played feature pictures for the first thirty minutes and says he worked steadily for eleven years.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Weekly, the news is going on. It's the news. I'm thinking of a guy in a theater. That music, Tassel never did. When I was a leader of the Liberty Theater, I had to feature my own pictures. I had to sit there with my first violinist and he'd have a tap. And I'd say, the theme this week, I'd pick out a nice theme for two lovers to clinch. We used to have a first and second theme, secondary theme. And I'd always close the curtain with my theme. And I'd talk it over with the manager who was a palomar. I'd say, how much of the feature do you want me to play? He'd say, you're going to play the first 30 minutes. So we'd sit there for 30 minutes. What went on in the middle, I never could tell you. I never used to look at it. But I directed some fine pictures. I directed way down east, Three Musketeers, Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse. You ever heard of them? I've heard of them. They were from Griffith, the road show pictures. They sent you a book. You had nothing to worry about except to have the musicians to play it. See? And then they'd put a screen up in front of it so they wouldn't know how few or how many we had behind it. But I usually insisted and got what I needed. If I needed a nobel player, I got one. Because they controlled the music. It was the singer that afterwards became Paramount Richards. And I was in the staff. I had to go along with them lots of times when I didn't want to go, but I was always secure. You know, musicians' life is not always the better roses, you know. They have weeks when they don't wake, you know. Got a long show of short. I was out of one day in eleven years. Is that a record?
I know you must have played in a lot of different kind of places to do that. No.
